intro: Welcome to Myra, an ancient city in Antalya province from the 5th century BC. This Lycian city is known for two things above all: its cliff of rock tombs and the church of Saint Nicholas.
history: Myra was one of the six great cities of the Lycian League. Then, in the 4th century, the tomb of its bishop Nicholas turned it into a pilgrimage centre.
structure-3: You are now at the Church of St Nicholas in Myra. The legend of its saint inspired Santa Claus, so a figure known far and wide traces back to this very place.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the rock-cut tombs and the Roman theatre, and then the Andriake harbour.
facts: Did you know? The rock tombs imitate wooden Lycian houses, with beams and doors carved into stone. They are, in effect, a photograph in stone of an architecture that has otherwise vanished. Saint Nicholas served as bishop here; his church stands in modern Demre, and his tomb was in it. And look at the theatre: it was rebuilt after an earthquake, and blocks from the toppled stage building still lie where they fell.
outro: This brings our tour of Myra to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. The faces of these tombs have watched over the city for centuries; let them keep watching. Enjoy your visit.
